claims.text: Localized friction stir processing can restore the structural integrity of damaged nickel-based superalloy turbine blades.
Localized friction stir processing can restore the fatigue life of damaged nickel-based superalloy turbine blades.
FSP can produce a homogeneous, fine-grained, recrystallized microstructure across the damaged region.
FSP repair will outperform traditional fusion-welding repair under aggressive operating conditions.
The damaged nickel-based superalloy regions considered are susceptible to hot cracking during fusion-welding repair.
Candidate FSP parameters include rotational speeds of 300–600 rpm and traverse rates of 50–100 mm/min.
Preliminary experiments on geometrically representative samples can identify an optimized tool design and FSP parameters.
Post-process heat treatment can relieve residual stresses after FSP repair.
Maintaining the substrate at or below 0.4–0.5 Tm keeps the FSP repair below melting while promoting dynamic recrystallization.
Severe localized plastic deformation during FSP induces dynamic recrystallization and grain refinement.
Avoiding a liquid phase during FSP prevents the hot-cracking mechanism associated with fusion welding.
Optimized tool design produces uniform material flow in complex component geometries.
Uniform material flow promotes a homogeneous microstructural repair.
The repaired interface will have a refined, uniformly recrystallized microstructure, reduced segregation, and minimal residual tensile stress.
The proposed repaired microstructure will provide mechanical continuity with the parent material.
Relative to fusion-welded specimens, FSP-repaired specimens will have longer fatigue life under cyclic thermomechanical loading.
Relative to fusion-welded specimens, FSP-repaired specimens will have improved crack resistance and delayed crack initiation.
Relative to fusion-welded specimens, FSP-repaired specimens will have lower residual stresses.
Traditional fusion-welding repairs of nickel-based superalloys suffer from hot cracking, high residual stresses, and reduced fatigue life under aggressive service conditions.
The repair is applicable to turbine-blade service loading provided that tool design and process parameters accommodate the component geometry.
